newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends weaker as Nov slips below $1,500.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends weaker as Nov slips below $1,500.

text.p: London's benchmark November coffee contract closed below nearby $1,500 support after origin and speculator selling finally managed to outstrip industry purchases earlier in the session, traders said on Thursday.
At a late stage November slipped below $1,500, moving below days of tight ranges and breaking its consolidation move and closed $23 lower at $1,495.
All other traded positions were weaker and total volume was 4,385 lots.
"There's some spec selling in London as well which is coming up against the industry buying," said one trader.
Market sources cited Far East selling, including Indonesia, as being responsible for the weakness, although industry buyers at around $1,500 had supported November's value through the day.

Earlier in the session, chart-linked selling pushed values lower, with stop-loss selling in anticipation of a weaker Arabicas open, but the losses were limited by scale-down roaster buying, traders said.
